outcome: Coagulation parameters (prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, D-dimer, platelet counts, fibrinogen levels, bedside clot formation)
cohort: The study included 200 pregnant women, comprising 96 patients diagnosed with preeclampsia and 104 healthy, normotensive controls.
finding: Women with preeclampsia exhibited significant coagulation abnormalities and thrombocytopenia, including higher prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, and D-dimer, and lower mean platelet counts and fibrinogen levels, indicating a progression toward a hypercoagulable state and a higher occurrence of postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: There were no statistically significant differences in the mode of delivery between the preeclampsia and control groups.
